convergence_level: pigment-pathway output rather than one universal gene
many_to_one_interpretation: Distinct genetic and regulatory perturbations at multiple positions in the anthocyanin/flavonoid network can converge on reduced chromatic pigmentation, providing a mechanistic accessibility explanation for recurrent white/nonwhite phenotype-space geometry.
important_bounds: five systems are a literature-verified mechanistic subset, not a random sample of angiosperms
Abronia fragrans provides a betalain-system counterexample to universal anthocyanin causation
the OpenTree test does not support a recurrent nonwhite-to-white evolutionary direction
environmental and pollinator comparative tests do not support one universal ecological driver
claim_ceiling: supports pathway-level many-to-one accessibility as a working mechanism; does not prove that this mechanism alone generated the global H2 geometry
